# Product of balls, two-limb center, with the special states

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_mul_2_full` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains $x y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$. A ball may also be the whole line or the empty set.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$, $c_w = c_{w0} + c_{w1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call its core, [`ball_mul_2`](ball_mul_2.md), instead.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand ball is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ and $Y$ are finite balls, and $\lvert (x y) - c_w\rvert \le r_w$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.
- **B4.** No condition under which $Z$ is a finite ball is claimed yet: the claims list none, which does not say that it always is.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $x y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_mul_2_full_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** ball_mul_2, then the fix-up of the special states of a ball (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** core: as ball_mul_2; fix-up: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_mul_2_full.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_mul_2_full.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_mul_2`](ball_mul_2.md).

```
# The product of balls with 2-limb centers, with the special states of a ball:
# ball_mul_2, then the fix-up of milestone1.md, "Ball kernels".

(cz0, cz1, rz) = ball_mul_2(cx0, cx1, rx, cy0, cy1, ry)
q              = add(rx, ry)
e              = eq(q, q)
a              = abs(cz0)
f1             = lt(a, const inf)
f2             = lt(rz, const inf)
f              = and(f1, f2)
c0             = select(f, cz0, 0)
c1             = select(f, cz1, 0)
r              = select(f, rz, const inf)
cw0            = select(e, c0, q)
cw1            = select(e, c1, q)
rw             = select(e, r, q)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
